official.deadline_note: No calendar date is published centrally. The MOE Operation Directions state that 'in principle, the application period is from February 1 to March 31 each year' and that 'the actual application period for each local representative office will, however, be the period announced in its publicly available guidelines', which each office must publish by January 31 each year. The 2026 round has closed; the next window follows the same February-March pattern.
official.application_cycle: Annual. The scholarship year begins on September 1 and ends on August 31 of the following year. Guidelines most recently amended by Ministry of Education order Tai-Chiao-Wen (V) Zi No. 1152500420A, promulgated 10 February 2026 and effective from the date of promulgation.
official.status_note: The programme runs on a fixed annual cycle whose window is in principle 1 February to 31 March. As of 10 October 2026 the official site shows no open call and no dated deadline for the next round; the most recent bulletin-board items are dated 22 January 2026 (lists of English-taught degree programmes and of universities giving tuition discounts, plus the MOE Terms of Agreement) and the Scholarship Guidelines page carries a publication date of 10 June 2026 with an update date of 10 February 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The MOE will pay up to NTD 40,000 each semester for each scholarship recipient's approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses. If these exceed a total amount of NTD 40,000, the remaining amount to be paid to the university or college must be paid by the student. The 'miscellaneous expenses' do not include administration fees, thesis supervision fees, insurance, accommodation, or internet access costs. These are the responsibility of the scholarship recipient.
benefits: Monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 for recipients undertaking a bachelor's degree and NTD 20,000 for recipients undertaking a master's degree or doctorate.
MOE pays up to NTD 40,000 each semester toward each recipient's approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses.
Universities and colleges may give scholarship recipients discounts for their tuition and miscellaneous expenses.

Recipients may apply for a working permit under the Regulations on the Permission and Administration of the Employment for Foreign Workers, with maximum work hours of 20 hours per week except during summer and winter vacation, and a maximum validity period of six months per semester.
eligibility: Each applicant shall be a foreign national who has a graduation certificate or diploma from a secondary school or post-secondary educational institution, an excellent academic record, and be of good moral character.
An overseas compatriot student or a person with R.O.C. nationality is ineligible, and students from the Mainland Area, Hong Kong and Macau are excluded.

A person who is already a registered student at a university or college in Taiwan, who is eligible to be admitted, or who has already registered to begin a degree program there is ineligible; a student in the final year of their current degree program applying for a higher-level degree is exempt from this restriction.

A person who has already studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level as the one applied for is ineligible, as is an exchange student or a dual or joint degree student admitted under an academic cooperation agreement between a Taiwanese and an overseas university or college.

A person who has already been a Taiwan Scholarship recipient for a total period of five years is ineligible, as is a person who has ever had a Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship revoked.

A person who will receive any form of financial assistance from any agency or organization of the Taiwan Government or any educational institution in Taiwan during their studies is ineligible, apart from a university or college discount covering tuition and miscellaneous expenses above the MOE subsidy limit.
requirements: Apply for admission directly to a university or college within the application period set by that university or college; each institution sets its own admission deadline.
Submit the application and all required documents to the representative office with jurisdiction over applications from the applicant's country of nationality.
Hold a graduation certificate or diploma from a secondary school or post-secondary educational institution, with an excellent academic record and good moral character.
Undertake a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree program.

Maintain the academic standard required to continue: a minimum average of 70 for bachelor's degree students and 80 for students at graduate research institutes each semester, or the higher standard set by the university, college, department or institute.
documents: A Taiwan Scholarship application form (each representative office designs the application form it uses).
A photocopy of the applicant's passport or other documentary evidence of their nationality.
A photocopy of their highest-level academic award and academic transcripts; documents in a language other than Chinese or English shall be accompanied by a notarized Chinese or English translation.

Photocopies of documentary evidence that the applicant has already applied to a university or college in Taiwan for admission for the approaching academic year (for example, a photocopy of the receipt for payment of the application fee, a photocopy of the application form, or a notice or email from the university or college acknowledging receipt of the application).

Two letters of recommendation, each written by a school principal, or university president, or college president, or professor, or tutor, and placed in an envelope which the person who wrote the letter seals and personally signs on the outside; plus any other documents specified by the representative office.
selection_criteria: Whether each scholarship recipient would be able to contribute to Taiwan's national development and become a skilled professional contributing to their own country and to Taiwan, by assisting in the growth of business and industry, the economy, and education.

An applicant whose GPA is on a scale with a highest possible score of 4.5 who wants to do a bachelor's degree shall have an average grade of at least 3.0, and an applicant who wants to do a master's degree shall have an average grade of at least 3.5; where the grading system differs, the representative office converts the average grade to its equivalent on a 4.5 scale, or selects outstanding students on the basis of academic results at or above a standard considered indicative of excellence by universities and colleges in that country or region.
The representative office shall thoroughly consider the person's personal circumstances, actual language proficiency, interpersonal manners, and moral character.
Preference is given to applicants with a TOCFL certificate at Band B level or higher, or evidence of equivalent score reports.

For a program completely taught in English: TOEFL test scores, or a certificate of having passed another intermediate level English language proficiency exam recognized by the government in that country or region, or documentary evidence of an overall score of at least 75%.
The application form shall be fully completed and submitted together with all the other documents; none of the submitted application documents will be returned.
coverage: Living allowance: NTD 15,000 per month for bachelor's degree recipients, NTD 20,000 per month for master's and doctoral recipients.
Tuition and miscellaneous expenses: MOE pays up to NTD 40,000 each semester for each recipient's approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses; any excess is paid by the student.
Universities and colleges may give scholarship recipients discounts for their tuition and miscellaneous expenses.
Scholarship recipients are responsible for the payment of all expenses apart from tuition and miscellaneous expenses.
No airfare or travel allowance is provided under the MOE Taiwan Scholarship.
application_method: Lodge the application at the representative office in the applicant's country of nationality, or the representative office responsible for handling applications from citizens of that country, during the period announced in that office's guidelines.
Contact information for overseas missions is published on the Official Website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Attend an interview conducted by the overseas mission.
Apply separately for admission to a university or college in Taiwan, and provide a copy of the admission notice to the overseas mission
Sign the Terms of Agreement for the MOE Taiwan Scholarship Program, agreeing to abide by the laws of Taiwan.
Obtain a health certificate meeting the items required for Health Certificate (Form B).
official.application_route: Lodge the scholarship file with the Taiwan Representative Office responsible for your country during its announced window, apply separately for admission to a Taiwanese university or college within that institution's own deadline, then hand your admission letter to the Representative Office by 30 June.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be foreign nationals. Overseas compatriot students and persons with R.O.C. nationality are ineligible, and students from the Mainland Area, Hong Kong and Macau are excluded. No residency rule is published.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The MOE Taiwan Scholarship exists specifically for outstanding students from outside Taiwan; only foreign nationals are eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field-of-study restriction is published; the directions apply to bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programs. The agency restriction is that applications must be lodged with the representative office in the applicant's country of nationality, or the representative office responsible for handling applications from citizens of that country. Recipients cannot enroll in specialized and vocational classes, and in-service degree programs are not covered.
official.duration: Four years for a bachelor's degree program, two years for a master's degree program and four years for a doctorate program. The total period that any one person is a scholarship recipient is not permitted to exceed five years. The scholarship year begins on September 1 and ends on August 31 of the following year; from the 2026 academic year onwards, living allowance payments for recipients beginning a bachelor's degree program are issued until June 30 of their graduation year.
official.description: The Ministry of Education has formulated these Directions to encourage outstanding students from outside Taiwan (with the exception of students from the Mainland Area, Hong Kong, and Macau), referred to as foreign students, to undertake degree studies in Taiwan, to familiarize themselves with the education environment in Taiwan, and promote exchanges, understanding, and friendship between Taiwan and the international community.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan))
official.english_requirement: For applications to undertake programs not fully taught in English, applicants shall submit a photocopy of their TOCFL test results or certificate of having passed at Band B (Level 3) or higher; test results or certificates from any other Chinese proficiency test will not be accepted. Where the representative office does not organize TOCFL testing, the applicant shall sit the TOCFL tests at their own expense by the end of their first semester of study in Taiwan and submit the Band B results to their university or college. For programs fully taught in English, the representative office may waive the TOCFL requirement and instead require TOEFL test scores meeting a standard it has set, or documentary evidence of passing a different English proficiency exam recognized by the local government, or documentary evidence of having graduated from a program fully taught in English; applicants who are citizens of a country where English is an official national language are not subject to this requirement.

study_mode: no full-time or part-time wording appears in the MOE Operation Directions or on the programme office pages

verification.notes: Read the full English text of the MOE Operation Directions Governing the Ministry of Education Taiwan Scholarships (order Tai-Chiao-Wen (V) Zi No. 1152500420A, promulgated 10 February 2026) on the Ministry of Education's own Laws and Regulations Retrieving System, plus the Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship Program Office pages for the scholarship comparison table, the application process, and the Application and Release, Languages and Courses, and Insurance and Housing FAQs. Stipend rates, the NTD 40,000 per-semester tuition cap and its exclusions, documents, selection floors, timelines and the five-year cap were all taken from the ministry's own pages; no aggregator was used.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the tuition-backed branch of the Taiwan Scholarship Programme, so it suits applicants who can win a place at a Taiwanese university as well as the scholarship, because the two applications run in parallel and only the university's own deadline governs admission. Budget for the semester before you fly: MOE caps tuition support at NTD 40,000 per semester and explicitly leaves accommodation, insurance, internet, administration and thesis supervision fees with you. If your programme is not taught entirely in English you need TOCFL Band B (Level 3) and no other Chinese test is accepted, so book that seat early. Applications go through the Taiwan Representative Office for your nationality, not through a central portal, so that office's locally published guidelines are the document that actually governs your deadline and paperwork.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong bachelor's, master's or doctoral applicants who are not from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau and are ready to run two applications at once for a Chinese-medium or English-medium Taiwanese degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the Taiwan Representative Office with jurisdiction over your nationality and obtain its locally published guidelines, which it must publish by 31 January each year; that document, not the central site, fixes your real deadline, quota and document list.
Start the separate university admission application first or in parallel, because the MOE directions require proof that you have already applied for admission when you lodge the scholarship file.
Book TOCFL Band B (Level 3) for a Chinese-medium programme, or TOEFL / a locally recognised intermediate English exam for a programme on the checklist of degrees fully taught in English.

Brief your two recommenders that each letter must be sealed in an envelope they personally sign across the flap, and that they must be a principal, university or college president, professor or tutor.
Arrange notarised Chinese or English translations of any transcript or award not already in Chinese or English.
Line up roughly one semester of cash plus a four-month travel health insurance policy before departure, since the first stipend can be delayed by accounting procedures.
common_rejection_risks: Lodging the scholarship file without documentary evidence that a Taiwanese university application has already been submitted, which is an express requirement of the MOE directions.
Failing to send the admission letter to the Representative Office by 30 June; anyone not admitted into a university or college has their eligibility revoked and the place goes to the waiting list.
Average grade below the published floor of 3.0 on a 4.5 scale for bachelor's applicants or 3.5 for master's applicants.
Holding any second government or university funding, which triggers full revocation and repayment of every stipend and tuition payment received.
Missing the TOCFL Band B deadline: the university suspends the living allowance from the following semester and revokes the scholarship from the third semester.
Being outside Taiwan for more than 15 days in a month, which allows the university to suspend that month's living allowance.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation, internet access, administration fees, thesis supervision fees, insurance, tuition and miscellaneous expenses above NTD 40,000 per semester, TOCFL registration fees (NTD 1,600 for the listening and reading tests), travel health insurance valid at least four months from arrival until National Health Insurance eligibility, student accident insurance of roughly NTD 200 to 300 per semester, and all international airfare, which the MOE award does not cover.
document_audit: The application form itself is designed by each Representative Office, so the version circulating on the central site is not necessarily the one your office will accept.
Recommendation letters must be sealed in an envelope the writer personally signs on the outside; an open or unsigned envelope is a published non-compliance.
Transcripts and awards in any language other than Chinese or English need a notarised Chinese or English translation, not a plain one.
For Chinese-taught programmes only TOCFL results are accepted; HSK or other Chinese proficiency certificates are expressly rejected.

Keep the proof of your university application (fee receipt, application form or the university's acknowledgement email) in the scholarship file, since it is a listed requirement rather than an optional extra.
alerts: There is no central dated deadline. The MOE publishes only 'in principle 1 February to 31 March', so a missed local Representative Office deadline cannot be appealed on the basis of the national window.
Winning the scholarship does not admit you. You must separately win university admission and hand the letter to the Representative Office by 30 June.
The five-year lifetime cap is counted across all degree levels, and you may not take a second award at the same or a lower level.
Awards can be withdrawn after arrival for low grades, absences above one-third of monthly classes, exchange semesters abroad, or an ARC not showing 'pursuing studies' as the reason for stay.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Lodge the file with your Taiwan Representative Office during its announced window, sit its interview and document review, then forward your university admission letter by 30 June; the office finalises the recipient list by 31 July and issues the award certificate, after which the Taiwanese university pays your monthly allowance once you register.

The page directs applicants to the Taiwan Scholarships and Huayu Enrichment Scholarships website for further information. The 2026 window has closed; the next is expected to follow the same February-March pattern.

The MOFA Taiwan Scholarship guidelines were last updated on 1 August 2023; the Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship Program Office's Scholarship Guidelines page carries a publication date of 10 June 2026.
official.status_note: The programme operates on a fixed annual window published as 1 February to 31 March. As of 10 October 2026 the MOFA guidelines page states no year for the current or next round and no open-call notice is posted; the most recent programme office bulletin-board items are dated 22 January 2026.

benefits: Monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programs.
Monthly stipend of NT$28,000 for the pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program (LEP).
One-way, economy-class plane tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan.
Insurance coverage provided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Taiwan Scholarship recipients who have signed the relevant personal data consent form, with all expenses borne by MOFA.
Universities and colleges may offer Scholarship recipients reduced tuition and miscellaneous fees.
eligibility: Is a high school graduate or above with an excellent academic record, of good moral character and has no criminal record.
Is not a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan) and is not an overseas compatriot student.
Has never attended an educational institution in Taiwan at the same level of degree or LEP that he/she intends to apply for.

Is not an exchange student through any cooperation agreement between a foreign university/college and an educational institute in Taiwan while receiving the Scholarship, and has not previously had a Scholarship revoked by an ROC government agency or other relevant institution.
The programme is not applicable to students from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau.
The Scholarship is, in principle, granted to students from countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan; special consideration may also be given to students from other countries.
requirements: High school graduate or above with an excellent academic record, good moral character and no criminal record.
Not a national of the Republic of China (Taiwan) and not an overseas compatriot student.

No prior attendance at an educational institution in Taiwan at the same level of degree or LEP being applied for, and no exchange student status under a university cooperation agreement while holding the Scholarship.
No previous Scholarship revocation by an ROC government agency or other relevant institution.

Recipients taking the pre-degree LEP must complete the language courses within the first year of the scholarship program; the LEP must be completed one year prior to the commencement of the degree program.

Submit a photocopy of the TOCFL transcript or certificate for Level 2 or above for degree programs taught in Chinese, and TOCFL Level 2 certificates for listening and reading by June of the year after arrival for LEP recipients.

Health certificate meeting the items required for Health Certificate (Form B).
Terms of Agreement for the MOFA Taiwan Scholarship.

Excellent academic record, good moral character and no criminal record.

Selection follows the programme guidelines published by MOFA, with first review and recommendation handled through the Taiwan Representative Offices, which use a published assessment form and recommendation list.

Monthly stipend of NT$28,000 for the pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program (LEP).
One-way economy-class plane tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan.
Insurance coverage for recipients who have signed the personal data consent form, with all expenses borne by MOFA.

application_method: Consult the MOFA Taiwan Scholarship guidelines published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Visit the Taiwan Scholarships and Huayu Enrichment Scholarships website, which the MOFA guidelines page names as the source of further information on the application process.
Contact information for overseas missions is published on the Official Website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Submit the application within the published window of 1 February to 31 March.

Apply separately for admission to a degree program leading to an undergraduate, master or doctoral degree, excluding in-service programs, or to a Mandarin Training Center affiliated with a university or college accredited by the Ministry of Education for the pre-degree LEP.
Contact person for the programme: Ms. Tina Shen, Tel +886-2-2882-4564 ext. 2396, Fax +886-2-8861-3491, email tina98@mail.mcu.edu.tw.
official.application_route: Read the MOFA guidelines, then apply through the Taiwan Representative Office for your country within the 1 February to 31 March window, using the Taiwan Scholarships and Huayu Enrichment Scholarships website for the full application detail and forms.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to non-Republic of China nationals who are not overseas compatriot students. Not applicable to students from mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau. In principle granted to students from countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, with special consideration for students from other countries.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The Scholarship aims to encourage outstanding international students to study in Taiwan and to promote bilateral exchanges and friendship between the peoples of Taiwan and its diplomatic allies.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field-of-study restriction is published. Degree programs are limited to undergraduate, master or doctoral degrees and exclude in-service programs. The pre-degree LEP must be taken at a Mandarin Training Center affiliated with a university or college accredited by the Ministry of Education.
official.duration: Pre-degree LEP: one year. Degree programs: undergraduate program four years maximum, master's program two years maximum, doctoral program four years maximum. Award periods must be continuous, with no breaks, and cannot exceed a total of five years.
official.description: These guidelines are stipulated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of China (Taiwan) for the implementation of the Taiwan Scholarship Program, which aims to encourage outstanding international students to study in Taiwan, as well as to promote bilateral exchanges and friendship between the peoples of Taiwan and its diplomatic allies.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan))
official.english_requirement: MOFA publishes no IELTS or TOEFL score requirement. The Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship Program Office's guidelines state that for those applying for degree programs taught in Chinese, a photocopy of a TOCFL transcript or certificate for Level 2 or above must be submitted, and that recipients of MOFA Taiwan scholarship shall at least pass TOCFL Level 2. Recipients taking the LEP must submit a photocopy of the TOCFL Level 2 certificates for listening and reading by June of the year after their arrival; those failing to do so will be disqualified from receiving the Scholarship for degree programs. Recipients pay the TOCFL fees themselves.

verification.notes: Read the MOFA Taiwan Scholarship guidelines in full on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' own site (en.mofa.gov.tw/cp.aspx?n=1325, guidelines updated 1 August 2023), then cross-checked the MOFA column of the Scholarship Comparison Table and the Languages and Courses and Insurance and Housing FAQs on the Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship Program Office site that the MOFA page names. Stipend rates of NT$28,000 for the LEP and NT$33,000 for degree programs, the one-way economy-class ticket benefit, the award periods and the eligibility clauses all come from the MOFA page itself.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the pure living-allowance branch of the Taiwan Scholarship Programme: NT$33,000 a month for a degree and NT$28,000 for the pre-degree Mandarin year, plus one economy-class ticket each way, and the guidelines are explicit that you carry everything else. Treat it as a stipend rather than a funded place, because tuition only falls if the university you win chooses to discount it, and that is discretionary. In principle it is aimed at citizens of Taiwan's diplomatic partners, so applicants from other countries are competing on a 'special consideration' basis and should verify their standing before investing in the paperwork. The application window is only stated as 1 February to 31 March with no year, so confirm the current round with the Representative Office for your country.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants from Taiwan's diplomatic partners, and strong candidates from other countries willing to be considered on a discretionary basis, who need a Mandarin year or a living stipend and can self-fund tuition and living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm whether your country has diplomatic relations with Taiwan or has been recognised by MOFA as having friendly relations, since that is the stated principle for the award.
Verify that you have never attended a Taiwanese institution at the same level of degree or LEP you are applying for; this is an absolute bar with no exception.
Obtain a TOCFL Level 2 transcript or certificate if your degree will be taught in Chinese, and diarise the June deadline for LEP recipients to submit Level 2 listening and reading certificates.
Sign the personal data consent form if you want MOFA's insurance coverage, which the FAQ says MOFA funds entirely for recipients who have signed it.
Raise the full first-year sum yourself: MOFA states recipients are responsible for all expenses during their stay in Taiwan.
Contact Ms. Tina Shen at the Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship Program Office (+886-2-2882-4564 ext. 2396, tina98@mail.mcu.edu.tw) for cycle-specific questions.
common_rejection_risks: Prior study in Taiwan at the same level, which is a flat disqualification under clause IV.4 of the guidelines.
Any criminal record, or a record that fails the good moral character test, which is an express eligibility condition.
Holding ROC nationality or overseas compatriot student status rather than foreign nationality.
Being an exchange student under a cooperation agreement between a foreign university and a Taiwanese institution while holding the Scholarship.
Assuming the ticket covers you both ways: the benefit is one-way economy-class for direct flights, and any additional or indirect travel is on you.
Counting on a university tuition discount that the guidelines describe only as something universities 'may' offer.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: All tuition and miscellaneous fees, accommodation, local transport, internet, and living costs beyond the NT$28,000 or NT$33,000 monthly stipend, plus any travel beyond the single one-way economy-class direct-flight ticket and any TOCFL registration fees (NTD 1,600 for listening and reading), which recipients pay themselves.
document_audit: The MOFA page itself lists no documents and simply points to the Taiwan Scholarships and Huayu Enrichment Scholarships website, so download the current MOFA Taiwan Scholarship Application Form from that site rather than reusing an old copy.
The health certificate must match the published items required for Health Certificate (Form B), which is a separate document from your routine medical check.
The Plane Ticket Application Form is a distinct form from the scholarship application; file it separately to claim the ticket.
LEP recipients must not let the one-year language year drift into the degree programme, because the guidelines require the LEP to be completed in the first year and before the degree starts.
alerts: Do not confuse this award with the MOE Taiwan Scholarship, which pays tuition up to NTD 40,000 a semester but gives no airfare, or with the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, which has no tuition component.
The guidelines attach no year to the 1 February to 31 March window, so the open dates must be confirmed with your Representative Office each cycle.
Award periods must be continuous with no breaks; pausing your studies is not an option if you intend to resume funding.
You may only receive one scholarship provided by the Taiwanese government or by a Taiwanese educational institution, so accepting another award voids this one.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through the Taiwan Representative Office for your country within the 1 February to 31 March window using the form published on the Taiwan Scholarships and Huayu Enrichment Scholarships site, attend the office's review and interview, and hold a separate university admission for the degree programme or a Mandarin Training Center place for the LEP.
